disease.name: Bacterial Wilt
disease.severity_index: Can cause up to 80% yield loss if untreated

environmental_factors.temperature_humidity: Prefers warm, humid conditions with high soil moisture
environmental_factors.soil_conditions: More severe in clayey and waterlogged soils

region_specific_information.Andhra Pradesh: Higher prevalence in coastal chilli farms with heavy rainfall
region_specific_information.Telangana: More common in irrigated farms with poor drainage

mid_stage: Dark brown streaks on lower stems
Yellowing of older leaves before complete wilting
advanced_stage: Brown discoloration of vascular tissues when stems are cut

soil_seed_treatment: Seed treatment with Streptocycline @ 0.5 g/L water before sowing
Basal application of Neem Cake @ 100 kg/acre to reduce bacterial load

cultural_practices: Improve soil drainage to reduce waterlogging risks
Remove infected plants immediately to prevent further spread
biological_control: Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 5 g/kg seed reduces bacterial infection
Bacillus mycoides soil application improves plant immunity
chemical_control: Copper Oxychloride @ 600 g/acre as foliar spray
Streptocycline @ 1 g/10 L water applied at root zone
Trichoderma viride soil drenching for disease suppression
